root_causes.description: product-catalog exhibits a severe, sustained server-side latency spike with p99 saturating at ~10000ms while CPU, memory, and error rate remain normal, indicating an injected/artificial latency fault in the product-catalog leaf service. Upstream callers (frontend, checkout, recommendation) inherit the added latency.

evidence.expected_baseline: p99 ~= 6 ms (healthy leaf service, e.g. cart p99=5.958 ms)
confirms ~6 ms is the normal server-side p99 for a healthy peer service
flat/normal CPU usage — rules out cpu_stress
flat/normal memory usage — rules out memory_stress / OOM
no error spike — rules out http_abort / dependency_failure
frontend latency elevated only because it calls product-catalog (downstream propagation, not origin)

root_causes.description: Frontend server-side latency is saturated at ~10000ms, but topology shows frontend calls product-catalog, so this is propagation of the product-catalog latency fault rather than an independent frontend fault.

evidence.expected_baseline: frontend p99 should track caller latency, not origin; elevated due to product-catalog dependency

root_causes.description: Checkout depends on product-catalog per topology; it can exhibit elevated latency from the same root cause, but no independent anomaly was confirmed for checkout in this window.

evidence.expected_baseline: healthy peer latency ~6 ms — bounds the fault to the product-catalog leaf, not shared infrastructure

remediation_steps: Inspect product-catalog deployment/config for an injected latency fault (e.g. flagd feature flag or chaos experiment affecting the catalog handler) and disable it.
Rolling-restart the product-catalog pods to clear any in-process artificial delay and confirm p99 returns to ~6 ms.
Verify recovery by re-checking product-catalog server-side p99 latency and confirming frontend/checkout latency returns to baseline.
Add/verify SLO alerting on product-catalog server-side p99 to catch latency injection early.
